title: SAM2 rare-object memory private fallback
hypothesis: On a synthetic SAM2 video with three visually similar objects and one object that changes appearance under occlusion, an online residual-triggered private memory fallback for at most one object/frame will keep mean propagated J&F within 1 pp of independent memory, improve by at least 5 pp over Givens-only memory, and use at least 25% fewer object-memory payload bytes than independent memory without using future masks.
physical_object: SAM2 per-object maskmem_features for each propagated frame
mirror_coordinate: Two per-object Givens angles over one shared per-frame mean memory plus a residual-energy gated full private slot for at most one object per frame
logical_multiplicity: Four stable object identities represented by one shared memory tensor, four small view codes, and sparse causal private fallback slots

upstream_assets.device: CPU; CUDA extension disabled per upstream CPU path

controls: Givens Mirror plus maximum-one private fallback
ID-switch count and fallback object IDs, reported without oracle future-mask error

development.selection_metric: development propagated mean J&F; tie-break on complete serialized bytes
development.allowed_tuning: Choose only the residual-energy threshold from [0.15, 0.30, 0.50, 0.80]. At most one object can receive a private tensor per frame.

fallback_rule: After each causal frame, compute each object's L2 residual norm against the common memory mean, normalized by the common mean norm. If the maximum score reaches the frozen threshold, store that object's full current memory feature privately; otherwise store no private memory. No future frame, ground-truth mask, future score, or predicted future error participates.

compute.active_compute: report encode/decode timing and allocated private-memory tensor count; full SAM2 propagation remains charged

success_gate: Across all 3 fresh worlds, fallback Mirror is within 1 pp mean J&F of independent, improves at least 5 pp over Givens-only in at least 2 worlds, uses at least 25% fewer serialized object-memory bytes than independent, and records zero additional ID switches versus independent.
failure_gate: Mirror misses the quality or object-memory-byte gate in at least 2 fresh worlds, or fallback spends the private slot on non-rare identities so often that the quality gate fails; report complete-session bytes regardless.
boundaries: one deterministic synthetic video per seed
no natural-video, benchmark, GPU, or general SAM2 claim
no oracle future-mask error or future ground truth for fallback selection
